title: Rust: Essential Vocabulary
name: Rust: Essential Vocabulary
description: The words you need to talk about Rust precisely.
key_points: Paradigm: A style of programming: procedural, object-oriented, functional, logic.
Typing: Static typing checks types before running; dynamic typing checks while running.
Compiler: Translates source code to machine code before execution.
Interpreter: Runs source code directly, line by line.
Garbage collector: Automatic memory cleanup in managed languages.
Standard library: Batteries-included modules shipped with the language.
Syntax: The grammar rules of the language.
Hello world: The traditional first program in any language.
REPL: Read-eval-print loop: an interactive prompt for trying code.
Package manager: Tool for installing third-party libraries.
Runtime: The environment a program needs to execute.
Type inference: The compiler deducing types you did not write down.

demo.program:
# Rust — self-test quiz demo
qa = [
    ("Who created Rust?", "Graydon Hoare (Mozilla)"),
    ("What paradigm is Rust?", "multi-paradigm"),
    ("What is creator?", "Graydon Hoare (Mozilla)"),
    ("What is first appeared?", "2010"),
    ("What is paradigm?", "multi-paradigm"),
    ("What is typing?", "static"),
    ("What is file extension?", ".rs"),
    ("What is hello world?", "println!(\"Hello, world!\");"),
]
score = 0
for i, (q, a) in enumerate(qa, 1):
    print(f"Q{i}: {q}")
    ans = input("Your answer: ").strip().lower()
    if ans and ans in a.lower():
        print("Correct.")
        score += 1
    else:
        print(f"Answer: {a}")
print(f"Score: {score}/{len(qa)}")
